question: Which one of the following constituents is present in hemoglobin A (HbA)?

A 64-year-old male presents to the hospital with excruciating back pain, His erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and creatinine levels are markedly raised. The clinical diagnosis made by the physician is multiple myeloma. What will be the most characteristic findings on his serum protein electrophoresis?

answers.option: Single sharp band in albumin region
Single sharp band in alpha region
Single sharp band in beta 2 region
Polyclonal broad band in gamma region
Single sharp discrete band in gamma region

question: The dead body of a young female is recovered from her house hanging from a fan. On examination it is seen that post mortem lividity in lower limbs is fully developed and fixed. If, in the dead body, the post mortem lividity does NOT blanch on applying pressure, what will be the probable time elapsed since her death?
A 16-17-year-old male has been sent to you for age determination. A radiograph of which of the following would be used for this purpose?
The lacunar variant of Reed-Sternberg (RS) cells is found in:
Which of the following chromosomes contain the gene for the beta-globin chain of hemoglobin?
Owl-like appearance is found in which cells present in Hodgkin lymphoma?

A male patient comes to you for a follow-up visit. He has a history of thromboembolism for which he was started on a low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH). However, he did not achieve adequate anticoagulation on LMWH. Therefore, he was started on warfarin. Which
of the following was most likely used to monitor the status of anticoagulation?
When is the first dose of the rotavirus vaccine administered?

A 14-week-old girl's parents are very concerned about her health and brought her to the EPI vaccination center. According to the EPI schedule, which of the following sets of vaccines will she be given?
In a bedridden patient, you are called to confirm the death. What is the surest and earliest sign of death?
An adult male is referred to you for age certification. He says he is 25 years of age. To confirm this age, which of the following should be radiographed?

A 6-year-old boy presents with history of fever and bloody diarrhea for the last 1 week. She has also had pallor and oliguria for one day. Laboratory findings show hemoglobin 5.5 gm/dL, TLC 6500/microlitre, platelets 30,000/mm³, and increased urea and creatinine. Peripheral smear shows target cells and schistocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-year-old lady presented with a history of on-and-off loose motion, pallor, and tingling sensations in her fingers. Examination: Anemia++, Jaundice+, otherwise unremarkable. CBC is showing HB 4.5, WBC 3.1, Platelets 73, MCV 123, MCH 32. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old lady presented with a history of severe pallor, shortness of breath, and weakness for 3 months. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. CBC is showing HB 4.5, WBC 8.7, Platelets 673, MCV 55, MCH 18. Peripheral film is showing hypochromic microcytosis and elliptocytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old lady presented with a history of severe pallor, shortness of breath, and weakness for 3 months. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. CBC is showing HB 9.5, WBC 8.7, Platelets 673, MCV 68, MCH 19. Peripheral film is showing hypochromic microcytosis and elliptocytes. She was diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia and prescribed oral iron replacement therapy. Which of the following is consistent with her treatment?

answers.option: 30% oral iron is absorbed of single dose
20% oral iron is absorbed of single dose
10% oral iron is absorbed of single dose
40% oral iron is absorbed of single dose
50% oral iron is absorbed of single dose

question: An 18-year-old lady presented with a history of pallor and tingling sensations in her fingers. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. CBC shows normochromic anemia, oval macrocytes, and hypersegmented neutrophils. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old lady presented with a history of pallor, weakness, lethargy, and shortness of breath. Her brother has transfusion-dependent anemia. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. CBC shows HB 4.5, WBC 4.1, Platelets 673, MCV 66, MCH 20. Peripheral film was showing hypochromia, microcytosis, and target cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old male presented with history of weakness, pallorness, lethargy and shortness of breath, confusion, headache, and low grade fever. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. CBC is showing HB 4.5, WBC 28.8, Platelets 33, MCV 104, MCH 34. Peripheral smear was showing Schistocytes 8.9%. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old baby presented with a history of pallor, lethargy, and bloody diarrhea. Examination: Anemia++. CBC is showing HB 4.5, WBC 37.8, Platelets 12, MCV 98,  MCH 31, Urea 121, Creatinine 3.9. Peripheral smear shows polychromasia, nucleated RBCs, and schistocytes 7.2%. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 43-year-old male presented with a history of weakness, pallor, lethargy, shortness of breath, confusion, headache, and low-grade fever. Examination: Anemia++ otherwise unremarkable. CBC shows HB 4.5, WBC 28.8, Platelets 33, MCV 104, MCH 34. Peripheral smear shows schistocytes 8.9%. Which diagnostic investigation will you suggest for this patient?

A 44-year-old male presented with a history of pallor, lethargy and shortness of breath, confusion, headache, and low-grade fever. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. CBC shows HB 5.1, WBC 21.3, Platelets 33, MCV 99, MCH 31, Urea 56, and Creatinine 2.1. Peripheral smear shows schistocytes 8.9%. Which of the following is the least likely possibility?
All of the following are associated with disseminated intravascular coagulation except?

A 6-year-old boy presented with a history of weakness, pallor, lethargy, and shortness of breath. Examination: Anemia++, otherwise unremarkable. He has a family history of congenital disorders. CBC shows HB 4.5, WBC 8.8, Platelets 738, MCV 58, MCH 19. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-month-old baby presented with a history of pallor, lethargy. Examination: Anemia++ and splenomegaly. He has a family history of congenital disorders. CBC shows HB 4.5, WBC 8.8, Platelets 733, MCV 58, MCH 19. Peripheral smear shows hypochromia, microcytosis, polychromasia, nucleated RBCs, and marked poikilocytosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-month-old girl presented with a history of pallor and low-grade fever. Examination: Anemia++. CBC shows HB 7.8, and peripheral smear shows hypochromic microcytosis, polychromasia, nucleated RBCs, and marked poikilocytosis. Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows HbA: 2.4%, HbA2: 3.1%, HbF: 94.5%. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which one of the following fibrinolytic inhibitors act via competitive inhibition of plasminogen activation?

A 54-year-old woman suffering from asthma was brought to the emergency room because of a sudden offset of left side paresis. Imaging studies confirmed the diagnosis of thromboembolic stroke and the patient started a treatment that included a drug that acts by blocking platelet ADP receptors. Which of the following drugs has this mechanism of action?

A 34-year-old man admitted to the hospital with the presumptive diagnosis of pulmonary thromboembolism started a treatment that included a drug that acts by accelerating the binding between antithrombin III and clotting factor proteases. Which of the following drugs has this mechanism of action?

A 27-year-old male patient, who you have been treating for the past 2 years after he was diagnosed with CHF caused by a viral cardiomyopathy. After being maintained on drug therapy for a year, the patient underwent a heart transplant procedure and is now being maintained on an immunosuppressive drug regimen consisting of cyclosporine, azathioprine, and prednisone. In addition, he is being treated with enalapril & hydrochlorothiazide, as well as valganciclovir. Which drug in this regimen exerts its therapeutic effects by selectively interfering with the activation of transcription factors involved in stimulating the transcription and production of IL-2?
A patient of chronic renal failure is maintained on intermittent hemodialysis. His anemia is not responding to iron therapy. Which of the following additional drug is indicated in this patient?

A 32-year-old patient attended the specialist complaining of feelings of fatigue, shortness of breath, and pallor that had been experienced over 3 months. She had recorded menorrhagia within the past 6 months. On examination, the pallor of the conjunctiva and the koilonychia are seen. She has hemoglobin 8 g/dL and MCV 70 fL. What is the next investigation supposed to be?

A 45-year-old male came to the emergency department complaining about swelling and pain in the left leg, which followed a long-haul flight. Deep vein thrombosis is confirmed using a Doppler ultrasound. Last year, he had such a situation when there was no reason. What is the most suited next test?

A 6-year-old boy has had recurrent nosebleeding and easy bruising over the last 6 months. The uncle tended to bleed as well. Platelet count is normal; APTT is prolonged. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old male with complaints of one month of fever, sore throat, and neck swelling. On examination, it is found that he has cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. Atypical lymphocytes exist on the peripheral smear. What do you think the diagnosis is?

A 28-year-old woman had the complaint of having jaundice and dark urine. She has the history of autoimmune disease. Labs demonstrate Hb of 9 g/dL, raised LDH, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and low haptoglobin. What will be the test that will confirm the diagnosis?
Which intestinal parasite is most likely to cause rectal prolapse and iron-deficiency anemia in cases of heavy infestation due to blood loss in the colon?
When the body makes its own antibodies in response to an infection or vaccination, What is this termed?

A low socioeconomic background 6-year-old boy is brought to the pediatric clinic by his mother due to fatigue, poor concentration, and reduced appetite for the past 3 months. He is pale on examination. His diet mainly consists of cow’s milk and biscuits, with very few fruits or vegetables. Laboratory findings: Hemoglobin: 8.0 g/dL, MCV: 68 fL, Serum ferritin: Low, Reticulocyte count: low. The mechanism of this child's anemia is:

answers.option: Blood loss due to parasitic infestation
Hemolysis due to red cell membrane defect
Autoimmune hemolysis leading to RBC destruction
Bone marrow infiltration due to leukemia
Decreased red blood cell production due to iron deficiency

question: A charred body Is brought for medico-legal examination after a house fire. The body is unrecognizable, and no personal belongings were found. The family insists it is their missing relative. Which of the following would be the most reliable method to establish personal identity in this case?

A partially decomposed body is recovered from a river, The skin is sloughed, and facial features are distorted. A finger has remained relatively intact. What should be the next best step to establish the identity of the deceased?

A skeletonized body is discovered in a deserted area. Forensic anthropologists are called to estimate identity. Pelvic bones and skull are present. Which of the following features would most reliably help determine the sex of the individual?

A skeletal mandible with intact third molars is recovered from a crime scene. A forensic odontologist is consulted to estimate the likely age of the individual at death. Radiological examination shows that the roots of the third molars are fully formed, but the apices are not yet closed. Based on the calcification stage of the third molars, what is the most probable age range of the individual?
A crime scene sample is subjected to DNA fingerprinting. The process involves cutting DNA into fragments. Which enzyme is primarily responsible for generating these fragments?
During DNA fingerprinting, a technique is used to separate DNA fragments based on size through an electric field. Which of the following best describes this method?
A dead body is highly decomposed. Tissue samples are not viable, but a tooth pulp sample is available. Which of the following is most appropriate for obtaining DNA from this source?
A latent print developed at a crime scene shows looping ridges that open toward the thumb side of the right hand. Which of the following describes this pattern?
Baby Iqra was born in a maternity home where she was given the BCG vaccine, Hep B and oral polio drops on the day she was born. Now she is 6-weeks-old and will be given the following vaccines:

A 5-year-old boy undergoes a routine tonsillectomy. However postoperatively achieving homeostasis is difficult. On further questioning of his parents they say he has always bruised easily. There is no family history of bleeding tendency and he has otherwise been well. A preoperative full blood count is normal. A clotting screen Is taken and shows: APTT 55s (normal: 35-45), PT 12s (normal: 10-14), TT 25s (normal: 23-24) Bieeding time 6 min (normal: 2-4) Factor VIII 0.6 U/ml (normal: 0.75-1.25). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old previously healthy child is brought to the clinic with sudden onset of bruises on the legs and small red spots over the trunk. There is no history of fever, joint pain, or recent medication use. The child had a mild viral illness two weeks ago. On examination, the child is active and afebrile. Petechiae and ecchymoses are noted. There is no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Blood counts reveal isolated thrombocytopenia. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old feel is brought to the pediatric ward with a 5-day history of bloody diarrhea, vomiting, and decreased urine output. On exam: BP 140/90 mmHg (hypertensive), HR 120/min, cap refill slightly delayed. Labs show: Hb 6.5 g/dL, schistocytes on peripheral smear, Platelets 45 x 10^9/L, Creatinine 3.0 mg/dL, BUN elevated, LDU high, haptoglobin low. She is oliguric, mildly edematous, and appears fatigued. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.option: Administer platelet transfusion to correct thrombocytopenia
Restrict fluids and monitor renal function only
Begin peritoneal dialysis and provide red blood cell transfusion
Start broad-spectrum antibiotics and antimotility agents

question: A previously healthy 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with fever, rash, and rapid breathing. He appears ill and lethargic. His temperature is 39.5C, HR 150/min, RR 40/min, BP 85/50 mmHg. Physical exam reveals purpura on his trunk and extremities, petechiae, and oozing from IV puncture sites. He is in compensated shock. Initial labs show: Platelets 40 x 10^9/L (low), PT prolonged, aPTT prolonged, Fibrinogen 0.8 g/L (low), D-dimer markedly elevated. Blood cultures are pending. He is started on intravenous fluids and broad-spectrum antiblotics. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.option: Give IV heparin to interrupt the coagulation cascade
Administer fresh frozen plasma (FFP) and cryoprecipitate to correct coagulopathy
Transfuse platelets only when bleeding increases
Withhold any transfusion until culture results confirm sepsis

question: A 4-year-old male is brought to the pediatric clinic with rashes on his arms and legs following minor trauma at the playground. History reveals that the mother is a known carrier of a hereditary bleeding disorder, and the father is also clinically affected by the same condition. Laboratory studies show a Factor VIII activity level of 2% of normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old male is brought to the pediatric clinic with several rashes on his arms and legs following minor trauma at the playground. History reveals that the mother is a known carrier of a hereditary bleeding disorder, and the father is also clinically affected by the same condition. Laboratory studies show a Factor VIII activity level of 2% of normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old male is brought to the emergency department with a persistent nosebleed. His medical history is unremarkable except for occasional easy bruising. Laboratory results are as follows: Bleeding Time: Normal, Clotting Time: Significantly prolonged. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old female presents to the student health center complaining of frequent, heavy nosebleeds and significantly prolonged bleeding after dental procedures. She also notes that her menstrual periods are consistently heavy and last for more than eight days. Laboratory evaluation reveals the following: Bleeding Time: Elevated, Platelet Count: Normal, Clotting Time: Mildly elevated, aPTT: Prolonged, Prothrombin Time (PT): Normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is considered the most cost-effective approach for managing and preventing the spread of worm infections in a population?

answers.option: Immediate isolation of the infected individual until three stool samples are clear
Routine monthly full-blood counts and peripheral smears for all children
Inpatient parenteral administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics
Surgical resection of the affected intestinal segment
Periodic mass drug administration (MDA) with a single dose of Albendazole

question: A child was diagnosed with pinworm infection. To ensure immediate management and successfully prevent reinfection within the household, which of the following is the most appropriate strategy?

answers.option: Prescribe a 7-day course of oral Metronidazole for the child and both parents.
Immediate isolation of the child and any immunocompromised household members for 7 days.
Administer a single dose of Albendazole to the symptomatic child only.
Treat the entire household with a single dose of an anthelmintic, repeated in two weeks, alongside strict hand hygiene.
Apply topical corticosteroid cream to the perianal area and observe for 48 hours before starting oral medication.

question:
This drug's mechanism of action involves reversible inhibition of inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH), leading to the inhibition of de novo purine synthesis, effectively depriving T and B lymphocytes of the nucleotides necessary for proliferation.

Which of the following medications is most likely being described?
Which of the following immunosuppressants causes inhibition of the transcription factor that causes IL-2?

A 52-year-old man presents to the urgent care clinic with a 2-day history of unilateral right calf pain and swelling. He recently returned from a 14-hour international flight. His vital signs are stable, and he has no history of active bleeding or recent surgery. After a duplex ultrasound confirms a Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) in the popliteal vein, which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

answers.option: Placement of an Inferior Vena Cava filter
Strict bed rest with leg elevation

question: A dead body was found in an apartment in such a state that its upper extremity and body were relaxed, but the lower extremities were rigid. What is the probable time since death?

A 28-year-old female was diagnosed with Budd-Chiari Syndrome when an abdominal Doppler ultrasound revealed extensive thrombosis in two of the three major hepatic veins. Further hematological workup reveals a primary Protein C and Protein S deficiency. After initiating initial management and stabilizing the patient, what is the most appropriate duration for anticoagulation therapy?

answers.option: Until hepatic vein recanalization is seen on imaging

question: A 55-year-old male underwent an emergency exploratory laparotomy following a motor vehicle accident. His post-operative course was complicated by prolonged immobilization in the surgical ward. On post-op day 10, he develops sudden-onset swelling and dull aching in his left calf. A compression ultrasound reveals a non-compressible popliteal vein, confirming a Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT). He has no prior history of clots and no known family history of thrombophilia. What is the most appropriate duration for anticoagulation therapy in this patient?

An 8-year-old male from East Africa is brought to the clinic with a rapidly enlarging, painless mass involving the mandible and maxilla. Physical examination shows significant facial distortion and loosening of the molars. A biopsy of the lesion reveals a dense sheet of small, non-cleaved lymphocytes with numerous interspersed tingible-body macrophages, creating a characteristic "starry sky" appearance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following systems measures height determined by the long bones?

A 32-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of chronic fatigue and "brittle nails." Upon further questioning, she admits to an unusual, persistent craving for chewing on large amounts of ice throughout the day. Physical examination reveals notable pallor of the conjunctiva and spoon-shaped concavity of the fingernails (koilonychia). Her medical history is significant for heavy menstrual bleeding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
According to the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) guidelines, at what ages should the oral Rotavirus vaccine be administered?
According to the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) guidelines, which vaccine is given at 9 months?
According to the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) guidelines, which vaccine is given at14 weeks?

A 58-year-old male presents with painless, "waxing and waning" lymphadenopathy over several years. A biopsy of an inguinal lymph node reveals crowded, back-to-back follicles that lack tingible-body macrophages. Immunohistochemical staining is positive for BCL-2 within the follicles. This overexpression of BCL-2, an anti-apoptotic protein, is most commonly caused by which of the following chromosomal translocations?
Which of the following bones is not routinely used for obtaining a bone marrow biopsy?
Which of the following sets of markers is most characteristically expressed in hairy cell leukemia?
How many years after disappearing is a person declared dead?

A 45-year-old male who recently emigrated from Southwestern Japan presents with generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and skin lesions. Laboratory studies reveal a significantly elevated white blood cell count and hypercalcemia. A peripheral blood smear shows atypical CD4+ T-lymphocytes with highly irregular, multi-lobed nuclei having a "cloverleaf" appearance. Which of the following viruses is the most likely causative agent of this patient's condition?

A 6-year-old child presents with bruising, petechiae, and bone pain. Laboratory studies reveal 80% lymphoblasts on the peripheral smear. A bone marrow aspiration is performed, showing a hypercellular marrow replaced by small blasts with scanty cytoplasm and inconspicuous nucleoli. Which of the following diagnostic approaches is most essential for establishing the definitive diagnosis?

A 10-year-old boy presents with progressive fatigue, pallor, and vague abdominal discomfort. His mother notes that he frequently plays barefoot in the soil behind their house and has recently complained of an intense itching sensation between his toes. Laboratory studies reveal a microcytic, hypochromic anemia and significant eosinophilia. Which of the following helminths is the most likely cause of this patient's presentation?

A 28-year-old male with known Sickle Cell Anemia is found to have a concurrent diagnosis of alpha-thalassemia trait. Which of the following describes the most likely clinical impact of the co-inheritance of alpha-thalassemia on this patient’s Sickle Cell Disease?

answers.option: It leads to a higher mean corpuscular volume
It increases the frequency of vaso-occlusive crises
It increases the rate of hemolysis
It has no significant clinical effect
It decreases the overall severity of the disease
